take: Jones has been making the same bag since 1971 and the restraint is the whole product. No legs, no cart strap, no panelling — a 2.9 lb carry bag with a three-way divider and an unstructured spine, which is why an Original off the shelf today still looks like the photographs from 1975. The 2011 owners found no patterns, no inventory and no factory, and reverse-engineered the shape from bags borrowed off old customers rather than redrawing it.

The Original at $125 in Burnt Clay is the proof piece. It is the cheapest bag they make and it is the same bag as the $215 Evergreen underneath — the price difference is material, not construction, which is a rare thing to be able to say about a range.

This is for the walker who wants the bag to disappear and does not need it to do anything else. The line runs $45 to $520 across 32 pieces, so a headcover or a ball pouch is an easy way to test the making before committing to a bag.
story_extra: Jones makes the best carry bag in golf by leaving things off it — no legs, no cart strap, no panelling to break the surface — and has been doing that from Portland, Oregon since 1971. The founding story is better than most because it is small. George Jones was a forty-year-old taxi driver who sewed the first bags in his basement and sold them out of the trunk of his cab. Jones still tells it that way on their own history page, and finishes the thought with a line that is hard to improve on: “Who could have known? George Jones, that’s who.”

What their site skips is the middle. George sold the company in 1990, and the new owners tried to make a Jones bag compete with the big manufacturers by making it less like a Jones bag. By the early 2000s the brand was effectively gone. The Lemman family and Chris Carnahan bought it in 2011, and what they bought was almost nothing: no patterns, no inventory, no factory. Matt Lemman, asked later what came with the deal: “Just the name, that was all.”

They reverse-engineered it from the bags that were still around Portland. Carnahan has said they gathered old ones from family and friends, and there were plenty to gather, because the bags last. They rebuilt to the original specifications in modern materials, which is why the Original still looks like the photographs from 1975 and weighs 2.9 lbs.

The current line runs from the $125 Original through the F-35 ripstop stand bags, the Rider cart bag, eighteen officially licensed school versions and the collaborations with PAYNTR, BEAMS and Lusso Cloud. One correction to something you will read elsewhere: Jones does not claim anywhere on its own site to have invented the single-strap carry bag.
